## Setting and conventions

- [P] Introduction (p. 1769): `X` is an `n x n` antisymmetric matrix of indeterminates over a field `K`, `K[X]` the polynomial ring in the entries `X_ij` with `i < j`, and `I_t = Pf_(2t)(X)` the ideal generated by all `2t`-pfaffians of `X`; the question is when the Rees algebra
  `R(I_t) = sum_(k >= 0) I_t^k T^k` is Cohen-Macaulay. The paper recalls that it is Cohen-Macaulay when `char K = 0` or when `n` is odd and `2t = n - 1` (citing Bruns, "Algebras defined by powers of determinantal ideals", (3.4)(b), and Eisenbud and Huneke,
  "Cohen-Macaulay Rees algebras and their specializations", Proposition 2.8), and aims at a positive answer outside the exceptional characteristic, which is `0 < char K <= min(2t, n - 2t)`. The case `n` even and `2t = n` is trivial.
- [P] Page 1769 (end): the term order `tau` on `K[X]` is induced by the variable order `X_1n > X_1,n-1 > ... > X_12 > X_2n > ... > X_23 > ... > X_(n-1,n)`; the Knuth-Robinson-Schensted correspondence (Knuth 1970) is the basic tool of Sections 2 and 3.

## Normality and primary decomposition (Section 1, pp. 1770-1771)

- [P] Proposition 1.1 (p. 1770), in non-exceptional characteristic, with `I_j` the ideal of `2j`-pfaffians and `I_j^(m)` its `m`-th symbolic power: `I_t^s = intersection_(j=1..t) I_j^(s(t-j+1))` is a primary decomposition of the `s`-th power. The paper attributes the three results to De Negri
  (reference [6]) and the pattern to Section C of Chapter 10 of Bruns and Vetter. Corollary 1.2: the powers of `I_t` are integrally closed. Corollary 1.3: the Rees algebra `R(I_t)` is normal.
- [P] Definition at the head of Section 1 (p. 1770): `I_j` is the ideal generated by all `2j`-pfaffians of `X`, so `I_1` is the ideal generated by the entries `X_ij`. Lemma 1.4 and its proof (p. 1770), for `2t <= n - 2`: the quotient of `R(I_t)` by `I_1 R(I_t)`, the ideal generated by the variables, is isomorphic to the `K`-subalgebra `S_t` of `K[X]` generated by the `2t`-pfaffians (citing Bruns, Lemma 2.2),
  `dim S_t = dim K[X]`, and so `I_1 R(I_t)` has height 1 in the Rees algebra and is a minimal prime over `I_t R(I_t)` (the scan does not let the subscript of the ideal in the printed statement be read with certainty; the isomorphism with `S_t` holds for the ideal of the variables, which is `I_1 R(I_t)`). Proposition 1.5 (p. 1770), for `2t <= n - 2`: `I_t R(I_t)` is a divisorial ideal with exactly `t` minimal primes `P_1, ..., P_t`, with `P_j intersect K[X] = I_j`, and `I_t R(I_t) = intersection_j P_j^((t-j+1))` is a primary decomposition. The proof is an induction on `t` using the argument
  of Jozefiak and Pragacz, Lemma 1.2 ([Jozefiak and Pragacz 1979](jozefiak-pragacz-1979-ideals-generated-pfaffians.md), p. 190). Remark 1.6 (p. 1771): any other associated prime of `I_t R(I_t)` contains all the `X_ij`.
- [P] Corollary 1.7 (p. 1771): the divisor class group of `R(I_t)` is isomorphic to `Z^t`, and the classes `[P_1], ..., [P_t]` form a system of generators (with a result of Simis and Trung); the `P_j` are the primes of Proposition 1.5, whose hypothesis is `2t <= n - 2`. Proposition 1.8 (p. 1771): for `S_t`, (a) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 it has rational singularities, (b) in characteristic 0 it is Cohen-Macaulay,
  (c) in non-exceptional characteristic it is a normal domain.

## A combinatorial result (Section 2, pp. 1771-1774)

- [P] Pages 1771-1772: for pfaffians the Knuth-Robinson-Schensted correspondence does not map the standard monomial basis of `I_delta` onto the ideal generated by the initial terms of the pfaffians that generate it; the example `n = 5`, `delta = [1245]` (p. 1772) shows `X_13 X_15 X_24`, the image of the standard monomial `[1235][14]` of `I_delta`, outside the ideal generated by the initial terms of the pfaffians that are not greater than or equal to `delta`; these are `[1234]` and `[1235]`, with initial terms `X_14 X_23` and `X_15 X_23`.
  Defined here: the shape of a product `nu` of pfaffians, `gamma_t(S) = sum_i (s_i - t + 1)_+`, and `gamma_t(M)` for a monomial `M` as the maximum of `gamma_t(nu)` over products `nu` of pfaffians with initial term `M`.
- [P] Theorem 2.1 (p. 1772): for a standard monomial `mu`, `gamma_t(mu) = gamma_t(KRS(mu))` for all `t`. Lemma 2.2, Remark 2.3 (p. 1773) and Proposition 2.4 (p. 1774) relate decreasing subsequences, the shape of the standard tableau and the shape of the monomial; they complete the proof of Theorem 2.1 and carry no separate statement used below.

## Cohen-Macaulayness of the Rees algebra (Section 3, pp. 1775-1777)

- [P] Page 1775: the `k`-th symbolic power `I_t^(k)` has a `K`-basis of the standard monomials `mu` with `gamma_t(mu) >= k`, a product `nu` of pfaffians lies in `I_t^(k)` exactly when `gamma_t(nu) >= k`, and `I_t^(k)` is the sum of the products `I_t^(k_1) I_(t+1)^(k_2) ...` over the admissible exponent sequences (formula (1) of the paper).
  Proposition 3.1: the products `nu` with `gamma_t(nu) = k` form a Groebner basis of `I_t^(k)` (for `tau`), and the initial ideal is generated by the monomials `M` with `gamma_t(M) = k`. Corollary 3.2: the initial algebra of the symbolic Rees algebra is finitely generated and normal, so it and the symbolic Rees algebra `R^s(I_t)` are Cohen-Macaulay.
- [P] Proposition 3.3 and Theorem 3.4 (p. 1776): if `char K = 0` or `char K > max_i(min(2 t_i, n - 2 t_i))`, then for the product `I_(t_1) ... I_(t_r)` the initial ideal is the intersection of the initial ideals of the symbolic powers; (a) the initial algebra of `R(I_(t_1) ... I_(t_r))` is finitely generated and normal, (b) `R(I_(t_1) ... I_(t_r))` is Cohen-Macaulay and normal, and
  (c) the associated graded ring of `K[X]` with respect to `I_(t_1) ... I_(t_r)` is Cohen-Macaulay. The proof is that of Theorem 3.6 of Bruns and Conca ("KRS, straightening, and powers of determinantal ideals"). For `r = 1` the theorem states that `R(I_t)` is Cohen-Macaulay and normal in non-exceptional characteristic, which is the statement announced in the introduction.
- [P] Remark 3.5 (p. 1776): the products of pfaffians that lie in a product `I_(t_1) ... I_(t_r)` need not form a Groebner basis of it; for `n = 9` and `char K = 0` or greater than 3 the paper exhibits a monomial of degree 6 that lies in the initial ideal of `I_2 I_4` and is the initial term of no product of pfaffians in `I_2 I_4` (the indices of the monomial are not reproduced here, since the scan does not let them be read with full certainty).
  Restricted to powers, a Groebner basis exists: for `Gamma_t(S) = max{k : gamma_j(S) >= k(t - j + 1) for j = 1..t}` and `Gamma_t(nu) = Gamma_t(S(nu))`, Theorem 3.6 (p. 1777): in non-exceptional characteristic the products `nu` of pfaffians with `Gamma_t(nu) = k` and `deg(nu) = k t` form a Groebner basis of `I_t^k`.
  Corollary 3.7 (p. 1777): in non-exceptional characteristic the products `nu` with `Gamma_t(nu) = k` and `deg(nu) = kt` for some `k` form a Sagbi basis for `S_t`, so the initial algebra of `S_t` is finitely generated and normal and `S_t` is a Cohen-Macaulay domain.

## Mapping to this repository

- [I] The A_5 fiber-cone program ([run rulebook](../../runbooks/run-rulebook.md), ledger rows A5-416, A5-418 and A5-421 in `docs/evidence/a5-exceptional-fibers/ledger.tsv`) computes the special fiber `R[It]/m R[It]` of the Rees algebra of Pfaffian-type ideals. For the generic ideal `I_t` of this paper the special fiber is the quotient of `R(I_t)` by the ideal of the variables, `I_1 R(I_t)`, and the proof of Lemma 1.4 (p. 1770), citing Bruns, Lemma 2.2, identifies this quotient with the subalgebra `S_t` generated by the `2t`-pfaffians. The generic fiber cone is therefore `S_t`, of Krull dimension `dim K[X]` for `2t <= n - 2`, and `S_t` is a normal Cohen-Macaulay domain in non-exceptional characteristic (Proposition 1.8 (c) and Corollary 3.7).
  The program's fibers have dimension at most 6 and arise from specializations of the generic matrix, which this paper does not treat.
- [I] Characteristic. The program works over `Q(i)` (characteristic 0) and modulo the primes 32009 and 32029. For 4-pfaffians (`2t = 4`) the exceptional characteristics are `0 < char K <= min(4, n - 4)`, a subset of the characteristics 2 and 3, so characteristic 0 and the primes 32009 and 32029 are non-exceptional for every `n`, and Theorem 3.4 (with `r = 1`), Proposition 1.1,
  Corollary 1.2 and Corollary 1.3 apply to the generic ideal there. The paper's statements are all for fields `K` with `X` generic over `K`; they do not compare the Hilbert function of the fiber over `F_p` with that over `Q(i)`.
- [I] What the paper does not give. (a) It treats the ideal generated by all `2t`-pfaffians of a generic alternating matrix of indeterminates, and products of such ideals. The program's ideals are generated by 4-pfaffians of specialized matrices (the entries are functions on a germ or a weight slice), so the Cohen-Macaulay, normality and Groebner basis statements transfer only by a hypothesis the paper does not supply:
  the paper's reference list includes the Eisenbud and Huneke paper on specializations of Cohen-Macaulay Rees algebras, which it cites (Proposition 2.8), together with Bruns (3.4)(b), only for the known Cohen-Macaulay cases (characteristic 0, or `n` odd and `2t = n - 1`), and proves no specialization statement. (b) It gives no defining equations of `R(I_t)` or of its special fiber `S_t`, no Hilbert function of `S_t`, and no description of the fiber over a stratum of the matrix; Theorem 3.6 describes a Groebner basis of the powers `I_t^k`, not a presentation of `R(I_t)`. (c) The term order `tau` is a fixed order on the entries; it is
  not the ordering of a Singular run. (d) The paper states no height or depth bound; the bound for the height of a Pfaffian ideal over an arbitrary Noetherian ring is Theorem 2.1 of [Jozefiak and Pragacz 1979](jozefiak-pragacz-1979-ideals-generated-pfaffians.md).
- [I] The registered sources on related Pfaffian and determinantal Rees algebras are [De Negri and Gorla](1303.6874.md) (invariants of Pfaffian ideals), [Bruns, Conca and Varbaro](1111.7263.md) (relations among minors) and
  [Bruns, Simis and Trung](bruns-simis-trung-1991-straightening-closed.md) (blow-up of straightening-closed ideals).
